name: PX4-Autopilot (NTNU fork, cbf branch)
summary: NTNU fork of PX4 whose cbf branch holds the actual PX4-CBF code: CBFSafetyFilter in mc_pos_control, a tof_obstacles_chunk uORB message and CBF_* parameters. Branch HEAD has only the analytic single-constraint filter; the FoV-constrained qpOASES QP is in the earlier commit 338fb51f.
why_it_matters: This is the code the PX4-CBF baseline must be copied from; its defaults and failure behaviour differ from the paper's flight values.
hackathon_notes: Fork (gh api fork=true), license BSD-3-Clause per gh api, last push 2025-05-06. Read src/modules/mc_pos_control/PositionControl/CBFSafetyFilter.cpp and multicopter_safety_filter_params.c. CBF_ENABLED defaults to 0. Parameter defaults (eps 0.5, kappa 10, alpha 1, p0 -2, LP gains 0.01) are not the paper's flight values. See docs/research/close-area-nav/05-cbf-baselines-faithful.md.

name: cbf_pc_selector
summary: ROS 2 node that turns depth images, range images or point clouds from one or more sensors into a small set of obstacle points for the composite CBF, by angular binning with a per-bin percentile filter.
why_it_matters: Defines the obstacle input the NTNU filter was tuned on; a faithful sim baseline should bin its range fan the same way.
hackathon_notes: License BSD-3-Clause per gh api, last push 2026-04-24. README read only. For a Python sim, copy the idea (bins_w x bins_h bins, percentile per bin, min/max range) rather than the node.

name: sample_based_bcbf
summary: Python code for the CDC 2025 sample-based belief CBF paper: simulation environments for tracking and collision avoidance and the belief-CBF policies.
why_it_matters: The only belief-CBF code found from the Vahs group; useful to check a re-implementation of the 2023 Gaussian BCBF baseline.
hackathon_notes: License MIT per gh api, last push 2025-07-21. README says to use a mamba environment from environment.yml; when time is short use a sample-local venv instead. Not run. Implements the sample-based variant, not the 2023 EKF version.

name: cyberpod_sim_ros
summary: ROS Melodic Segway simulation used for the CoRL 2020 measurement-robust CBF results, with a virtual camera stream and the ECOS SOCP solver.
why_it_matters: Reference code for the MR-CBF baseline: shows how the authors set up the SOCP filter and the learned estimator.
hackathon_notes: No license field per gh api, so read-only. Last push 2020-12-31, default branch perception. ROS Melodic on Ubuntu 18.04; do not try to run it under time pressure, read it.
